..summary: Four agents copy the same subscribe->spawn->envelope->span->process runtime while agent-core's runtime abstractions have zero production callers

evidence: Each agent main.rs repeats the same ~50-line runtime: tracing_subscriber init, clap Config, async_nats::connect, ConnectorConfig::from_env, nats.subscribe(SUBJECT_X), `while let Some(msg)` spawn-per-message envelope parse + info_span + process (detection-agent/main.rs:209-280, triage-agent/main.rs:362-413, hunt-agent/main.rs:181-248, response-agent/main.rs:371-429) plus the identical emit() helper

agent-core exports AgentLoop + CheckpointStore + PostgresCheckpointer + ToolGateway + Budgets, yet no production code outside the crate instantiates any of them — the intended shared boundary is bypassed in favor of per-binary machinery

api-server creates agent_checkpoints (a2a.rs:221-228 'owned by agent-core') and joins it in load_task/load_run (a2a.rs:320-346, acp.rs:159-180) to detect completed runs, but nothing writes the table — a generated-but-never-fed data path; docs/services.md:75-77 promises 'agent loop checkpoints to Postgres so restart resumes, not restarts', which is unimplemented
detail.suggestion: Extract the shared agent runtime where it belongs: add an `emit_activity`/subscribe-and-dispatch helper to agent-core (or the new activity contract module) and have the four agents adopt it; then either wire PostgresCheckpointer into a real agent loop or delete the checkpoint join in api-server and the resume-on-restart doc claim so the boundary reflects reality.

..summary: agent-core promises the agent runtime but has no role in the running system, so 'where does an agent live?' has no answer

evidence: crates/agent-core/src/lib.rs:1-7 and Cargo.toml describe the crate as 'Agent control loop, checkpointing, tool gateway and kill switch for ARES'
AgentLoop::new has zero non-test callers; HttpToolGateway, PostgresCheckpointer, Budgets, CheckpointStore, AgentError and LoopOutcome appear nowhere outside crates/agent-core (grep over crates/)

The only exports reaching production code are kill_switch_engaged (api-server/kill.rs, triage/response/vuln-agent) and the AgentState/Step types read as a DB column in api-server/src/a2a.rs:320 and api-server/src/acp.rs:159
Each of the five agents instead hand-rolls its own subscribe/spawn/LLM/tool-invoke body in main.rs (triage 413 LOC, response 429, detection 280+293, hunt 248, vuln 322)
detail.suggestion: Pick one owner for agent execution and make the crate honest about it: either wire AgentLoop/HttpToolGateway/PostgresCheckpointer into the agents (which also gives one resilience policy for /invoke), or delete agent_loop.rs, gateway.rs, budget.rs and checkpoint.rs and move AgentState/Step into agent-protocol next to Envelope, leaving agent-core as the kill-switch module or removing the crate. Do not leave a capability crate whose entire surface is unimported.

..summary: ACP landed as a second 634-line protocol front-end in api-server with no matching change to the sibling crate's shape, the rate-limit tiers, or the docs

evidence: The two protocol crates have asymmetric responsibilities: a2a owns the dispatcher and the TaskBackend seam (crates/a2a/src/rpc.rs:135-157), acp owns wire types only (crates/acp/src/lib.rs:1-11), so all ACP lifecycle logic (ensure_schema, load_run, wait_terminal, SSE, cancel) sits in api-server/src/acp.rs

acp.rs reaches into a2a internals (crate::a2a::AgentDef, task_uuid, terminal_step, build_payload) rather than through a shared abstraction, so the second protocol is a sibling module of the first rather than a peer

Adding ACP required no update to crates/api-server/src/ratelimit.rs:37-45 — POST /a2a/* is Expensive but /acp/runs falls through to Tier::General, under-metering the LLM-backed run path that the rate table was written to protect (docs/services.md:97)
docs/services.md rate and contract sections gained no ACP rows (docs/services.md:94-101)
detail.suggestion: Make the two protocols peers: give acp the same shape as a2a (a transport-agnostic dispatcher + a backend trait in the acp crate, implemented by api-server) so both crates own their protocol and api-server owns only transport/persistence. Extend classify() with the ACP run/SSE routes in the same edit that adds a route, or drive tiers from the router table so the next protocol cannot skip them.

..summary: The agent roster (name, subject, envelope kind, activity name) is declared in three places and is already incomplete — vuln-agent is not in it

evidence: crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:76-124 hardcodes AGENTS with subject + EnvelopeKind + activity_name + skills for exactly four agents ('The four invocable Ares agents')
crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:49-58 separately encodes the same EnvelopeKind -> subject mapping (route_subject), so routing knowledge has two owners that can disagree silently
crates/agent-protocol/src/lib.rs:16-26 holds the subject constants but not the roster, and vuln-agent declares its own subjects locally (crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:27-29)
vuln-agent is a full pipeline agent (322 LOC, publishes advisories, opens cases) that never entered AGENTS, so it is invisible to /a2a/agents, /acp/agents and the well-known cards
detail.suggestion: Put the roster in agent-protocol next to the subject constants (name, subject, kind, activity name, description) and have both api-server's cards and orchestrator's route_subject read from it; then adding an agent is one entry, and the compiler forces the router and the interop surface to agree. Add vuln-agent as part of that move.

..summary: Cargo manifests split 7/14 between brace-style workspace deps with metadata and dotted-style without

evidence: a2a, acp, agent-core, agent-protocol, audit, cvss, llm-client declare `serde = { workspace = true }` plus a `description` and `rust-version.workspace = true` (e.g. crates/a2a/Cargo.toml:6-14).
The other 14 declare `serde.workspace = true` with no `description` and no `rust-version` (e.g. crates/connectors/Cargo.toml:9-16, crates/api-server/Cargo.toml:6-26).
The split is not lib-vs-bin: connectors, enrichment-lib, http-limits and policy-engine are libraries that follow the bin style, so 4 of 11 libraries contradict the other 7.

`#![warn(missing_docs)]` tracks the same 7-crate group (present in agent-protocol:8, agent-core:9, a2a:8, acp:9, audit:12, llm-client:8; absent from cvss, connectors, enrichment-lib, http-limits, policy-engine), so the doc-completeness lint covers only part of the library surface.

agent-core/Cargo.toml:17-19 and audit/Cargo.toml:15-17 both re-declare sqlx inline with a comment explaining that the workspace spec requests a nonexistent `pgvector` feature — a documented workaround that leaves two crates outside the centralised-dependency convention.
detail.suggestion: Pick one manifest style (dotted is the majority at 14/21) and apply it to all 21 crates, add `description` to the 14 that lack one, and add `#![warn(missing_docs)]` to the five libraries that already document everything by hand.

..summary: Three agents re-implement the LLM completion + fence-strip + parse sequence with different fence handling

evidence: detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:32-56, triage-agent/src/main.rs:105-127 and response-agent/src/main.rs:136-157 each build a `CompletionRequest`, call `router.complete`, then hand-roll `.trim().trim_start_matches("```json")...trim_end_matches("```")` before parsing.

The three copies have already diverged: pipeline.rs:48-50 also strips ```yaml and ```yml (needed for Sigma drafting) while the two JSON consumers strip only ```json and ``` — so an uppercase ```JSON fence or a ` ``` json` variant is handled by none of them.

llm-client (the crate that owns provider interaction) exposes no helper for this, so each agent re-derives the protocol; detection-agent/src/pipeline.rs:35 and response-agent/src/main.rs:139 are also flagged as a boilerplate-duplication pair.
detail.suggestion: Add one `llm_client::complete_json<T: DeserializeOwned>(router, tier, req) -> Result<T>` (or a `strip_fences` + `complete_text` pair, ~15 lines) that strips an optional case-insensitive fence with an optional language tag, and call it from the three sites.

..summary: Documented `{error: string}` envelope is honored only by the rate limiter; siblings return plain text, bare status, or `{code, message}`

evidence: docs/services.md:37-38 states the contract: "Errors: JSON `{error: string}`; 4xx = caller fixable, 5xx = retryable."
15 handlers in crates/api-server/src/main.rs, vulns.rs, playbooks.rs and coverage.rs return `(StatusCode, String)` (e.g. main.rs:125, vulns.rs:73), which axum serializes as text/plain — not JSON.

crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:50-56 and its nine `(StatusCode, Json<AcpError>)` sites return `{code, message}`; crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:508-513 returns a bare `StatusCode::NOT_FOUND` with an empty body while a2a.rs:548 returns `(StatusCode, String)`.
crates/ingestion-gateway/src/main.rs:110-121 returns `{id, status, error}` and uses 502 where docs/services.md:36 specifies 503 when NATS is down.

Internal failures are reported as gateway errors: `list_audit` (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:197) and `get_plan` (main.rs:268) map Postgres errors to BAD_GATEWAY, so a 5xx no longer tells the caller whether to retry a dependency or report a server bug.
detail.suggestion: Add one `ApiError` type in api-server implementing `IntoResponse` (status + `{error}` body, internals logged not echoed) and convert the 15 `(StatusCode, String)` handlers plus the ACP/a2a error returns to it; that is fewer shapes than exist today, not more.

..summary: `process` names the whole per-envelope handler in two agents while three sibling binaries use distinct, descriptive verbs

evidence: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:253 `async fn process(deps: &Deps, envelope: &Envelope)` runs IOC extraction, enrichment, the LLM verdict, case creation and handoff
crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:235 `async fn process(deps: &Deps, envelope: &Envelope)` builds a plan and executes every action
Siblings name the same concept concretely: `run_cycle` (crates/detection-agent/src/main.rs:138), `run_sweep` (crates/hunt-agent/src/main.rs:131), `handle_message` (crates/orchestrator/src/main.rs:61)
The triage call site reads `process(&deps, &envelope).instrument(span).await` (main.rs:404), giving no hint of what is processed or into what
detail.suggestion: Rename both to `handle_envelope` (or `triage_envelope` / `respond_to_envelope`) and use one verb for the per-envelope entry point across the five binaries, so a reader moving between agent crates finds the same name for the same role.

..summary: `Impact::{Read, Write, High}` mixes an access kind with an intensity, so `Impact::High` reads wrong at every guard

evidence: crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:69-73 `pub enum Impact { Read, Write, High }` — two variants classify access, the third classifies severity
crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:375 `if tool.policy.impact != Impact::Read` reads as "not read" but means "write or high impact"
The YAML vocabulary in policies/tools.yml uses `high` alongside `read`/`write`, so the wire value is fixed even if the Rust variant is clarified
detail.suggestion: Rename the variant to `HighImpact` (keeping `#[serde(rename = "high")]` so policies/tools.yml is unchanged) so the enum reads as one axis: Read, Write, HighImpact.

..summary: Two insert-and-report helpers return bools with opposite meanings (true = duplicate vs true = newly inserted)

evidence: crates/orchestrator/src/dedupe.rs:33-41 `check_and_mark` inserts the key and returns `Ok(res.rows_affected() == 0)`, i.e. true means already seen
crates/vuln-agent/src/main.rs:161-185 `record_advisory` inserts the advisory and returns `Ok(inserted.is_some())`, i.e. true means new
The orchestrator call site needs the doc comment to disambiguate: `Ok(true) => { info!("duplicate alert; skipped") }` (orchestrator/src/main.rs:94-98)
detail.suggestion: Put the polarity in the name: `mark_seen_and_report_duplicate` in dedupe.rs (still true = duplicate) and `insert_advisory_if_new` in vuln-agent, so both call sites read correctly without consulting the docstring.

..summary: Executor structs drift from the tool names they serve, and only 2 of ~20 carry a `Tool` suffix

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:564 `struct NvdTool` and :633 `struct CvssScoreTool` are the only two executor types with a `Tool` suffix; the rest are MispSearch (:183), ThehiveCase (:103), WazuhAgents (:314), SlackNotify (:532)

crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:649 `struct DryRun` is the stub executor for tools with no backend; its name describes the JSON payload it returns (`dry_run(args)` at :35) rather than the executor
crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:103 `ThehiveCase` serves the tool name `thehive.case.create` (returned at :108), so the type name and the tool name diverge
The registry at :668-779 pairs each type with a different tool name in some cases (MispAttribute serves both `misp.attribute.add` and `misp.ioc.block`)
detail.suggestion: Drop the suffix (`NvdLookup`, `CvssScore`) so all executors follow the verb/noun pattern of their neighbours, rename `DryRun` to `StubExecutor`, and make each struct name a readable contraction of the tool it registers (`ThehiveCaseCreate`).

..summary: Tool argument names drift per executor and are masked by alias lists of two to six keys

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:194 and :241 the MISP search tools accept `["value", "ioc", "query"]` for the same argument
crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:398 ProviderLookup accepts `["ioc", "value", "ip", "domain", "hash", "url"]` — six names for one input
crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs:177 CortexAnalyzer accepts `["data", "observable"]` and :131 accepts `["case_id", "id"]`, so no single canonical name exists per concept
detail.suggestion: Declare one canonical argument name per concept in each executor's doc comment (`ioc`, `case_id`, `data`) and trim the alias lists to canonical + at most one legacy spelling, so a developer or planner prompt has a single name to target.

..summary: Triage passes the case id to response only inside a thehive:// URI; the receiver defaults the id to "unknown"

evidence: Producer: crates/triage-agent/src/main.rs:218-223 carries the case id only as ref_uri: format!("thehive://case/{case_id}") with kind: "case"; no field on Artifact or HandoffPayload holds an identifier.

Consumer: crates/response-agent/src/main.rs:175-186 recovers it with find(|a| a.kind == "case").strip_prefix("thehive://case/")...unwrap_or_else(|| "unknown"), so any producer that changes the URI scheme silently degrades to the literal "unknown".
That literal then becomes response_actions.case_id (response-agent/src/main.rs:319) and the TheHive case patched at line 347, so a mismatch writes plan data under a case that does not exist.
detail.suggestion: Add a typed case identifier (or a CaseRef struct) to HandoffPayload/Artifact so the id crosses the boundary as data; keep ref_uri purely for retrieval.

..summary: api-server returns three different error-body shapes (plain text, typed ACP error, empty) despite one documented contract

evidence: docs/services.md:37 states the contract: 'Errors: JSON `{error: string}`; 4xx = caller fixable, 5xx = retryable.'
Console/vuln/playbook handlers return `(StatusCode, String)` -> `text/plain` bodies (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:111-137, vulns.rs:49-121, playbooks.rs:70-82).
ACP handlers return `(StatusCode, Json<AcpError>)` with `{code, message, data}` (crates/api-server/src/acp.rs:51-56).
`GET /a2a/{agent}/.well-known/agent.json` returns a bare `StatusCode::NOT_FOUND` with no body (crates/api-server/src/a2a.rs:508-511).

`GET /coverage` returns HTTP 200 with a `note` field when the content directory is unreadable (crates/api-server/src/coverage.rs:22-28), so failures are indistinguishable from empty coverage without key sniffing.
Only the kill-switch handler emits an `error` key (crates/api-server/src/kill.rs:66-70), and it adds a `path` field no other endpoint has.
detail.suggestion: Add one `ApiError` type to api-server (e.g. `(StatusCode, Json<ApiError{error: String}>)` with `impl IntoResponse`) and make every handler, including a2a's `agent_card` and `coverage`, return it; keep ACP's `{code,message,data}` only behind the `/acp` prefix where the spec requires it, and convert coverage's 'cannot read' case into a 500.

..summary: Tool arguments are specified twice — JSON Schema in policies/tools.yml and alias lists in executors — and no schema is exposed by the API

evidence: 17 tools carry `args_schema` with `additionalProperties: false` (policies/tools.yml:32-38,42-47,81-116,122-167), so only the canonical key names can ever reach an executor.

Executors nonetheless accept undocumented aliases: `arg_str(args, &["value", "ioc", "query"])` (executors/mod.rs:190), `&["case_id", "id"]` (:126), `&["q", "query_string"]` (:97), `&["cve_id", "id", "cve"]` (:583), plus shape polymorphism ('`{case_id, observable}` or flat fields', :131-136) and `values` vs `value` fallbacks (:280-296).
The trait exposes no schema: `fn name()` + `async fn execute(&self, args: &Value)` (executors/mod.rs:36-38).

`GET /tools` returns names only (`Json<Vec<String>>`, crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:208), and `PolicyEngine` keeps validators private, exposing only `tool_names()` (crates/policy-engine/src/lib.rs:305).
detail.suggestion: Add `fn schema(&self) -> Option<&serde_json::Value>` to the `Tool` trait (or have tool-server serve the policy's `args_schema`), return `[{name, schema}]` from `GET /tools`, and drop the alias lists from the executors so policy YAML is the single arg contract.

..summary: AuditWriter::append takes six positional parameters, four of them adjacent &str, and takes the decision as a string

evidence: `pub async fn append(&self, actor: &str, tool: &str, args: &Value, decision: &str, reason: &str, correlation_id: Uuid)` (crates/audit/src/lib.rs:59-67) — six parameters, with `actor`/`tool`/`decision`/`reason` all plain `&str`.

Callers must pre-convert the domain enum: `decision_label(&decision.kind)` at crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:90-98, and the reject path hardcodes the literal `"deny"` (crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:349).
Transposing `decision` and `reason` compiles silently and corrupts the hash-chained row; the audit table is the tamper-evident record, so a mis-order is unrecoverable.
detail.suggestion: Replace the parameter list with one struct — `AuditEntry { actor, tool, args, decision: DecisionKind, reason, correlation_id }` — so the compiler enforces field names and the enum, and delete `decision_label` from the call sites.

..summary: Reject path hardcodes the "deny" decision label instead of the shared decision_label()

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/main.rs:63-69 centralizes the audit vocabulary in decision_label().
crates/tool-server/src/approvals.rs:252 calls crate::decision_label(&decision.kind) on approve, but approvals.rs:304 passes the literal "deny" on reject.
The label is a query key for audit_log rows (crates/api-server/src/main.rs:187-197 returns `decision` verbatim), so a typo or rename in one path silently splits the audit vocabulary.
detail.suggestion: Replace the literal with crate::decision_label(&DecisionKind::Deny) so both approval outcomes go through the single label function.

..summary: agent-core ships ~545 LOC of framework (AgentLoop, HttpToolGateway, CheckpointStore, Budgets) that no binary instantiates

evidence: grep for `agent_core::` outside the crate returns only `kill_switch_engaged` (api-server/main.rs:39, kill.rs:9, response-agent:22, triage-agent:24, vuln-agent:18) and the `AgentState`/`Step` types read by api-server (a2a.rs:320-329, acp.rs:159-167).

`AgentLoop` (agent_loop.rs:93), `HttpToolGateway` (gateway.rs:57), `CheckpointStore`/`PostgresCheckpointer`/`InMemoryCheckpointer` (checkpoint.rs) and `Budgets` are exported from lib.rs but never constructed by any service; each agent hand-rolls its own loop instead.

Nothing writes `agent_checkpoints` in production: the only INSERT is checkpoint.rs:62-72 inside the unused `PostgresCheckpointer`, while api-server creates and reads the table (a2a.rs:222, 321; acp.rs:160), so the `Step::Final` folding at a2a.rs:328-346 and acp.rs:167-179 can never fire.

The documented retry contract in gateway.rs:1-90 (MAX_RETRIES, full-jitter backoff, retryable hint) is not in effect: response-agent/src/main.rs:210-232 posts to `/invoke` with no retry and its own duplicated `InvokeResponse { decision, result }` struct (response-agent:190 vs gateway.rs:27).
detail.suggestion: Either wire the agents through `AgentLoop`/`HttpToolGateway` (making checkpoints real and deleting the per-agent invoke code), or delete agent_loop.rs, gateway.rs, checkpoint.rs and budget.rs and keep agent-core to kill.rs + state.rs. The middle state — published framework nothing calls, plus read paths that can never fire — is the expensive one.

..summary: ~9% of all lines are doc comments, most restating the identifier they document

evidence: `#![warn(missing_docs)]` in six crates (agent-protocol/lib.rs:8, a2a/lib.rs:8, llm-client/lib.rs:8, audit/lib.rs:12, agent-core/lib.rs:9, acp/lib.rs:9) forces a doc line on every public item, including struct fields.

Result: `/// Agent name.` above `pub name: String` (a2a/src/card.rs:47, acp.rs:107), `/// The plan text.` above `text` (agent-core/src/state.rs:14), `/// The observation text.` (:24), `/// The final answer text.` (:29), `/// The text payload.` (a2a/src/task.rs:87), `/// Optional session id.` (acp.rs:109), `/// Terminal time.` (acp.rs:119).

Trivial constructors get prose: `/// Create a router from a fast and a strong provider.` on `new(fast, strong)` (llm-client/src/lib.rs:120), `/// Empty queue.` on `Store::new` (approvals.rs:74), `/// Create a writer bound to `pool`.` on `AuditWriter::new` (audit/src/lib.rs:48).
1279 `///` lines total against 14,394 LOC; the comments that do add value (policy order, TTL rationale, retry budget) are a small minority.
detail.suggestion: Drop `#![warn(missing_docs)]` to module/type level (or keep it for public APIs but not fields) and delete the restating one-liners. Keep the docs that carry a constraint — the order of policy checks, the 72h TTL rationale, the dry-run contract.

..summary: Infallible serialization is guarded with unwrap_or_default, turning bugs into empty 200 bodies and empty SSE data

evidence: acp.rs:342: `serde_yaml::to_string(&manifest).unwrap_or_default()` — `AgentManifest` derives `Serialize`, so failure is impossible; if it ever happened the endpoint would answer 200 with an empty YAML body.
a2a.rs:592 and a2a.rs:598: `serde_json::to_string(&task).unwrap_or_default()` — same derived-`Serialize` situation, producing an empty `task` SSE frame.
a2a.rs:379 and acp.rs:229 use the same `unwrap_or_default()` shape when serializing a message that always serializes.
27 `unwrap_or_default()` call sites in the workspace; the ones above are the defensive subset guarding pure expressions rather than genuine `Option`/parse boundaries.
detail.suggestion: Serialize these infallible values once at the top of the handler (or use `serde_json::to_string(&x).expect("Task is Serialize")`) so a failure is loud, instead of emitting an empty body that looks like a valid empty response.

..summary: agent-core's AgentLoop/ToolGateway/CheckpointStore runtime has zero production consumers; every agent hand-rolls its own loop

evidence: A grep for AgentLoop, ToolGateway, HttpToolGateway, CheckpointStore, PostgresCheckpointer and InMemoryCheckpointer across crates/ returns hits only inside crates/agent-core/src (agent_loop.rs:64,70; gateway.rs:36,47; checkpoint.rs:11,49) — no service crate constructs any of them.

The only implementors are test doubles: agent_loop.rs:218 `EchoGateway` implements ToolGateway and agent_loop.rs:232 uses `InMemoryCheckpointer`, so the runtime is exercised solely by its own unit tests.

crates/agent-core/src/lib.rs:3-8 documents AgentLoop as the way ARES agents run, which contradicts every agent's actual main.rs (triage-agent/src/main.rs:329-337, response-agent/src/main.rs:198-206, detection-agent/src/main.rs:62-63).

The new API's storage contract is bypassed too: api-server reads checkpoints with raw SQL (`SELECT state FROM agent_checkpoints WHERE thread_id = $1`) at a2a.rs:320 and acp.rs:159 instead of `PostgresCheckpointer`.
detail.suggestion: Resolve the dual path in one direction. Either delete AgentLoop/ToolGateway/CheckpointStore/Budgets plus their tests (crates/agent-core/src/{agent_loop,gateway,checkpoint,budget}.rs) and let agent-core keep only kill switch, state and error, or migrate triage-agent and response-agent onto AgentLoop + HttpToolGateway first and then retire their hand-rolled loops. Also point api-server's two checkpoint reads at `PostgresCheckpointer` so the table has one reader contract.

..summary: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs is 1189 LOC holding 7 external API clients, config and HTTP helpers with no submodule boundary

evidence: One module defines OpensearchClient (line 130), ThehiveClient (214), CortexClient (277), MispClient (429), WazuhClient (562), ShuffleClient (649) and NvdClient (885), plus ConnectorConfig (683) and the shared retry/send helpers (79-128).

Because there are no module names to point at, docs/services.md:128 has to cite raw line numbers for it (`connectors/lib.rs:695-740`, `lib.rs:773`), which is the navigation cost of the monolith in practice.

The scan evidence flags it as the top complexity hotspot (928 LOC at scan time, complexity score 85) and it is the crate with the most consumers (api-server, tool-server, bas-runner, detection-agent, hunt-agent, response-agent, triage-agent, enrichment-lib).
detail.suggestion: Turn lib.rs into a facade and split by upstream system: http.rs (Auth, env, join, json_ok, retry_sleep, send_with_retry), opensearch.rs, thehive.rs, cortex.rs, misp.rs, wazuh.rs, shuffle.rs, nvd.rs (incl. parse_cve/parse_cve_page) and config.rs (ConnectorConfig), with `pub use` re-exports so no caller changes. Move in that order (helpers first, then one client per commit), validating with `cargo test -p connectors` after each step and `cargo build --workspace` at the end.

..summary: executors/mod.rs keeps 20 of 21 tool executors inline while only openshell.rs is extracted

evidence: crates/tool-server/src/executors/mod.rs is 816 LOC and contains 20 `impl Tool for ...` blocks (OpensearchQuery, ThehiveCase, ThehiveCaseUpdate, ThehiveObservable, CortexAnalyzer, MispSearch, MispAttribute, MispAttributeSearch, MispEventView, MispWarninglist, MispSighting, WazuhAgents, WazuhActiveResponse, ShuffleWorkflow, ProviderLookup, EntraUser, SlackNotify, NvdTool, CvssScoreTool, DryRun) plus the Tool trait, arg helpers, build_registry (674) and missing_executors (788).
Only `mod openshell;` (line 8) follows the one-file-per-executor pattern, so a developer adding an executor has two competing precedents and no rule for which to follow.
The module docstring states the invariant 'Every entry in policies/tools.yml maps to one Tool implementation', but the file gives no per-executor boundary to verify that mapping against.

..summary: WazuhClient::token holds the token mutex across the authenticate HTTP round-trip

evidence: crates/connectors/src/lib.rs:621-641: `let mut guard = self.token.lock().await;` then `send_with_retry(req).await` (which retries with full-jitter sleeps under a 15s `CALL_BUDGET`, lines 88-140) and `json_ok(resp).await` all execute while `guard` is alive; it is only written at line 637.

detail.suggestion: Fetch the token outside the lock (authenticate is idempotent) and only take the mutex to store it: check `self.token.lock().await.clone()`, drop the guard, do the request, then `if guard.is_none() { *guard = Some(token) }`. ..summary: Gateway comment says rate limiting is outermost; the layer chain puts auth outermost

evidence: main.rs:159-160 applies `.layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(rl, ...))` then `.layer(middleware::from_fn_with_state(auth, ...))`; in axum the last layer is outermost, so `auth::middleware` runs before `http_limits::middleware`.
The comment at lines 157-158 asserts the opposite: 'Rate limiting outermost so unauthenticated floods are still metered; authentication then gates everything except the exempt paths.'
crates/api-server/src/main.rs:383-388 relies on the correct rule ('CORS stays outermost') when it puts `CorsLayer` last, so the two files disagree about ordering semantics.
Consequence: unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401 before the limiter sees them, so unauthenticated floods are not metered and only authenticated traffic consumes buckets.
detail.suggestion: Swap the two `.layer` calls so the rate limiter is applied last (outermost), or fix the comment to state that auth runs first; pick one and make the comment match the code.

..summary: Audit hash uses nanosecond timestamp, verification re-hashes the microsecond DB value

evidence: lib.rs:103-109 builds the canonical string with `ts = ts.to_rfc3339()` where `ts = Utc::now()` (nanosecond precision), then hashes it.

The same `ts` is bound into a `timestamptz` column (lines 111-128); PostgreSQL/sqlx store microseconds, so the value read back differs from the hashed one whenever the sub-microsecond digits are non-zero.
verify_chain (lines 161-180) recomputes the canonical string from the stored `row.ts.to_rfc3339()`, so it reports `broken_at` with 'hash does not match row contents' for essentially every intact row.
detail.suggestion: Truncate the timestamp before hashing and storing, e.g. `let ts = Utc::now().trunc_subsecs(6)` (or hash `ts.timestamp_micros()`), so the canonical string is identical on insert and verify.

..summary: NVD 404 is detected by substring-matching a formatted error message

..summary: Non-2xx /invoke responses become a synthetic 'deny' policy verdict

..summary: bas-runner passes dry=false to execute(); its dry-run branch is unreachable

evidence: main.rs:197-203 returns early from `run_scenario` when `deps.dry`, so the later `execute(scenario, deps.dry)` at line 204 is only reached with `dry == false`.

..summary: `denied` is unwrapped from an Option that is always Some

evidence: main.rs:241-242 builds the tuple `(Some(v.decision), v.result)` in the only success arm; the error arm returns early at line 274.
main.rs:277-280 then computes `decision.as_ref().map(|d| d.kind == DecisionKind::Deny).unwrap_or(false)` — an unwrap_or on a value that cannot be None.
main.rs:293-294 also stores `decision.as_ref().map(|d| d.kind)` and `decision.as_ref().map(|d| d.reason.clone())`, adding an Option layer to the persisted record for no reason.

..summary: Kill-switch halt breaks the loop and then reports 'done' with a Final checkpoint

evidence: main.rs:215-223 publishes the `kill_switch` activity and `break`s, so execution continues to the summary block.
main.rs:345-356 then publishes `done` ('{n} actions executed') and `save_final_checkpoint`, which writes `Step::Final`.

..summary: Blast-radius counter increments before the cap check, so denied calls consume the quota

evidence: lib.rs:412-416 increments `ctx.counters` and returns the new count before any check runs.
lib.rs:417-427 compares `count > max` afterwards, so the call that is rejected has already been counted.

lib.rs:428-442 returns early on cooldown before the cooldown timestamp is written, but the hourly counter increment from line 414 is not rolled back, so repeated denied attempts can exhaust the hourly budget for legitimate calls.
detail.suggestion: Read the current count, decide, and only increment on the allow path (or increment-and-compare but roll back the increment on every deny branch).

..summary: No database-backed test harness: every Postgres store is untested while its in-memory twin is tested

evidence: `idempotency.rs:183` `Store::pg` and `:188` `Store::mem` are documented as 'identical semantics', but all 9 tests (lines 424-545) drive only `mem` and the pure `Record` helpers; `claim_pg`'s `INSERT .. ON CONFLICT` reclaim/expiry SQL (lines 217-320) is never executed.
